blocks.text: You have studied the basics of Mendelian genetics in Grade X. This chapter carries the concept forward to post-mendelian research. It also gives an insight into the inherited diseases and their symptoms and treatment.

blocks.title: Recalling
blocks.text: The Austrian monk, Gregor Johann Mendel, was the first to explain the mechanism of inheritance. He developed true-breeding (pure-breeding) varieties of pea plants. A plant which is true-breeding for a particular trait produces all the offspring with the same trait upon self-fertilization.

Mendel performed monohybrid crossed in pea plant. In the first monohybrid crosses, he observed the inheritance of “seed shape”. When he crossed a true-breeding round-seeded plant with wrinkled-seeded plant, all plants of F1 generation produced round seeds. He called the trait that expressed in the F1 plants (round seeds) as dominant and the alternative trait that was not expressed in the F1 plants (wrinkled seeds) as recessive trait.

When F1 plants were self-pollinated, the 1/4 of F2 seed were wrinkled. In other words, the dominant-recessive ratio among the F2 seeds was 3 dominant : 1 recessive. His results suggested that the 3:1 ratio in F2 generation was really a disguised 1:2:1 ratio.
